scene: Your salon needs music. A slaver offers two Thracian flute-girls at a price that is really a favor; a free Ligurian harpist offers herself for wages and a room.

choices.label: Buy the Thracians
choices.resultText: They play beautifully and cost nothing after tonight. The slaver now considers you a friend, which is its own cost.

choices.label: Hire the Ligurian
choices.resultText: She plays songs the patrons have never heard and understands every word they say about her. You compare notes weekly.

scene: The widow of a former Archon calls on you, veiled, and asks you to teach her daughter how to hold a room. She cannot be seen to have asked.

choices.label: Teach the girl, discreetly
choices.resultText: Three afternoons on how to listen. The girl marries well and never mentions you. Her mother does, to the right people.

choices.label: Name a fee worthy of the secret
choices.resultText: The widow pays, and remembers being made to. The girl does very well anyway.

scene: Two poets come to blows at your table over which of them you smiled at. One is talented; the other is a Kleitos.

choices.label: Side with the talented one
choices.resultText: The Kleitos leaves without his cloak. The poem the other one writes about the evening is very good and names no one.

choices.label: Side with the Kleitos
choices.resultText: The talented one leaves. The Kleitos sends a gift. The poem he writes about the evening is bad and names you.

scene: A Carthaginian factor wants a place at your table on the regular terms. His silver is excellent; his accent, in your salon, is a statement.

choices.label: Admit him
choices.resultText: He pays in Punic silver and talks in Punic freely, assuming no one understands. Someone does.

choices.label: Refuse him, gracefully and publicly
choices.resultText: The refusal is repeated at every old family's table. So is the grace.

scene: The city has decided your salon is a shop. The assessor is at the door with a stylus and a look that says he knows what an evening here costs.

choices.label: Show him honest books and pay
choices.resultText: He is surprised the books exist. He is more surprised they are honest. He assesses you fairly, once.

choices.label: Show him the other books
choices.resultText: He assesses you as a modest musician. He also, on his way out, asks about Thursday.

scene: A love-letter in your hand, addressed to a married councilor, is going round the barbers' quarter. You never wrote it. The hand is very good.

choices.label: Find the forger and expose her
choices.resultText: A rival's scribe, bought with a bracelet. You return the bracelet to the rival in front of her table.

choices.label: Claim it, and improve on it
choices.resultText: You recite the letter at your own table with better lines. The councilor's wife stops coming to the agora. He does not stop coming to you.

scene: A girl from the harbor quarter, all elbows and eyes, stands at your door and says she wants to learn what you know.

choices.label: Take her in
choices.resultText: She learns the lyre, the silence, and the arithmetic. In five years she is your rival and your heir, and you are proud of both.

choices.label: Send her to the temple with a coin
choices.resultText: She goes to the temple, or somewhere. You think of the elbows and eyes now and then.

scene: A philosopher wants to write you into a dialogue, as the wise woman who teaches the young men about love. He will change your name, a little.

choices.label: Allow it, and correct his Greek
choices.resultText: The dialogue circulates as far as Athens. The name is barely changed. Strangers quote you at you.

choices.label: Refuse; you are not a character
choices.resultText: He writes it anyway with a worse woman in it. Everyone knows. You are, in a sense, still in it.

scene: An old patron is dying and has written you into his will: a house by the harbor. His sons stand at the foot of the bed, doing sums.

choices.label: Accept the house
choices.resultText: The house is yours after a year of lawyers. The sons never greet you again. The house has a fine view of their warehouse.

choices.label: Release the bequest to the sons
choices.resultText: The sons, astonished, send a gift larger than the rent. The city hears of a hetaira who refused a house, and doesn't know what to do with it.

scene: A Salyan chief wants an evening at your salon. He will pay in cattle. The old families will pay in gossip.

choices.label: Host him, in style
choices.resultText: He is courteous, enormous, and recites a poem about a river. Your patrons are outraged for a week and curious for a month.

choices.label: Refuse; cattle do not fit through the door
choices.resultText: He sends a torque anyway, with no note. You wear it, once, to see who notices.

scene: A councilor asks you to keep his rival drinking at your table until the morning's vote is over.

choices.label: Agree, for a price and a favor
choices.resultText: The rival wakes at noon, having missed the vote and had a wonderful evening. The councilor owes you and knows it.

choices.label: Warn the rival instead
choices.resultText: The rival goes to bed early and wins the vote. He sends flowers. The councilor sends nothing, pointedly.

scene: By law, women in Massalia drink water. A magistrate arrives during a symposium to inspect what is in your cup.

choices.label: Show him water, and a smile
choices.resultText: Water, all evening, in a cup that everyone knows held wine at sundown. He inspects the smile longest.

choices.label: Offer him a cup of what you're drinking
choices.resultText: He drinks it. He fines you. He comes back the next week without the stylus.

scene: The Dionysia announces a lyre contest open to women of the city. Hetairai are not named as excluded, which is not the same as included.

choices.label: Enter and play
choices.resultText: You place second to a citizen's daughter who is genuinely better. The judges look relieved. The crowd is not.

choices.label: Coach the citizen's daughter instead
choices.resultText: She wins with your fingering. Her father does not know who taught her. Her mother does.

scene: A young man you declined has been drinking at your gate for three nights, promising to burn the door. His father is on the council.

choices.label: Hire men and let him see them
choices.resultText: He sees the men and goes home. His father hears about the men and sends an apology and a jar of oil.

choices.label: Send for his father yourself
choices.resultText: The father comes at midnight and takes his son home by the ear. He owes you a discretion, and knows the price of one.

scene: A man you knew when you were seventeen offers to sell you a letter you wrote then. He has a copy, of course.

choices.label: Pay him
choices.resultText: You pay. He is back in a year. You knew that when you paid.

choices.label: Tell him to publish it
choices.resultText: He publishes it. It is a very good letter. Three patrons ask whether you still write like that.

scene: A house in the upper city is for sale, among the old families. No hetaira has lived there. The seller needs silver more than he needs neighbors.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.resultText: You move in at dawn. By dusk, two neighbors have complained to the Ephors and one has called with figs.

choices.label: Let the harbor keep you
choices.resultText: The house sells to a Rhodian. The old families complain about him instead.

scene: The priestesses of Artemis, who do not speak to hetairai, send a girl to say you may attend a women's rite at the temple, veiled, once.

choices.label: Attend, veiled and silent
choices.resultText: Incense, a hymn you knew as a child, and a priestess who nods at you very slightly. You are not asked again, and it is enough.

choices.label: Decline; you know what one rite is worth
choices.resultText: The girl returns your answer. The priestesses, you hear, expected it.

scene: A man with Syracusan manners offers steady silver for steady whispers about which hulls sail west, and when.

choices.label: Sell him harbor gossip
choices.resultText: Harmless gossip, you tell yourself. A hull is taken off Sardinia the next month, and you stop telling yourself.

choices.label: Report him to the Ephors
choices.resultText: He is gone before the guards arrive. The Ephors' clerk begins coming to your salon, on the city's silver.

scene: Your maid has counted her savings and asks, with a jar in her hands, whether it is enough to buy herself.

choices.label: Free her, and take less than the jar
choices.resultText: She stays on for wages and cries at your door once a year on the anniversary. Your patrons find this unbearably charming.

choices.label: Tell her the price has risen
choices.resultText: She puts the jar away. She is very good at her work and never looks at you the same way.

scene: You learn that your chief rival is a runaway slave from Syracuse with a forged manumission. Her patrons include half the council.

choices.label: Keep it, and let her know you have it
choices.resultText: She sends a gift monthly and takes no patron you want. The arrangement is never spoken of and never breaks.

choices.label: Bury it, and tell no one
choices.resultText: She never learns what you know. You learn that some secrets are a kind of weight you can carry.

scene: A wealthy patron proposes to set you up as a landowner in Olbia: groves, a house, respectability, and the end of the salon.

choices.label: Refuse, and mean it
choices.resultText: He is hurt, then relieved, then generous. The salon has never been so well attended as the month after.

choices.label: Say you will think about it, and keep him thinking
choices.resultText: Olives are discussed monthly. So is the rent of the house you have not moved to.

scene: A candidate for Archon wants to spend the night of the vote at your salon, where the results will reach him first and the wine second.

choices.label: Host his night
choices.resultText: He wins. The first thing the new Archon does is thank his hostess in front of forty men.

choices.label: Stay neutral; the loser will still need somewhere to drink
choices.resultText: He wins somewhere else. The loser drinks at yours for a month, and talks.

scene: A captain from Alexandria offers Arabian perfume at cost, in exchange for an introduction to the harbor master's brother.

choices.label: Make the introduction
choices.resultText: The perfume sells itself. The introduction leads to a contract you were not told about, and a second jar.

choices.label: Buy the perfume outright, no introductions
choices.resultText: Full price. The captain respects it and tells other captains that this hetaira cannot be bought with perfume.

scene: A guest collapses at your table. The other guests are already saying the word 'poison', quietly, and looking at the cups.

choices.label: Send for a physician in front of everyone
choices.resultText: Bad oysters. The physician says so loudly. The word 'poison' lingers in one house only, the one that said it first.

choices.label: Move him to a back room and hush it
choices.resultText: He recovers. No one speaks of it. Everyone thinks of it, at your table, for a season.

scene: A satirical song about the Ephors is being sung in every tavern. The Ephors have asked who wrote it. You know exactly who: he wrote it at your table.

choices.label: Say you have never heard the song
choices.resultText: The poet is grateful in verse. The Ephors are unconvinced in prose.

choices.label: Give them the name
choices.resultText: The poet is fined and stops coming. The song, now that everyone knows who wrote it, is sung twice as much.

scene: A sculptor wants you to model for an Aphrodite bound for a sanctuary in Sicily. Your face on a goddess, forever, on an island that will never know your name.

choices.label: Sit for him
choices.resultText: Marble, and your face on it, sailing west. Pilgrims will pray to your cheekbones for a thousand years.

choices.label: Decline; a goddess should not owe you
choices.resultText: He uses another face. It is a fine statue. You go to see it before it sails, and are sure yours would have been better.

scene: Three women who hear everything, a fishwife, a bath-attendant, and a priestess's maid, propose that what they hear should come to you first, for a share.

choices.label: Accept, and pay them well
choices.resultText: By the second day of anything, you know it. By the third, someone is paying you to know it.

choices.label: Decline; a network is a leash
choices.resultText: They take the offer to your rival. Her salon is very well informed for a year, and then very well watched.

scene: An Ephor has taken to arriving after the other guests leave, and talking. Not about you. About everything.

choices.label: Listen, and keep it
choices.resultText: He talks until dawn, once a week. You hold the city's business in your head and never spend a word of it. That is the price and the prize.

choices.label: Listen, and spend a little of it
choices.resultText: One word, sold once, buys a house. He notices something has moved in the city, and stops arriving late.

scene: A jewel is missing after last night's party. Your slave girl is accused by the guests. You saw a patron's hand pocket it.

choices.label: Name the patron
choices.resultText: He returns it laughing, calling it a joke. He does not return himself. The girl looks at you as if you were something new.

choices.label: Let the girl take the blame and lose the jewel
choices.resultText: The patron keeps coming, generously. The girl keeps her eyes down. You keep the account.

scene: A patron offers you his family's seat at the theatre for the Dionysia, in the front, where his wife sat last year.

choices.label: Take it, and dress for it
choices.resultText: The whole theatre sees you sit. The play is Euripides, which helps.

choices.label: Decline; there are seats he can give you that his wife did not own
choices.resultText: He is stung, then thoughtful, then sends a better gift. His wife, you hear, sends a smaller one, anonymously.

scene: A patron you dropped has started saying, at every table in the upper city, that you are older than you were and dearer than you are worth.

choices.label: Answer with a season no one can call cheap
choices.resultText: Musicians from Syracuse, wine from Chios, and a month that empties the strongbox. The upper city talks about the season instead of your age. For a season.

choices.label: Let him talk
choices.resultText: He talks. Some listen. Two patrons find younger salons and a third finds he misses yours, later, which does not pay the rent now.

scene: The harbor fever finds your house. You recover, but slowly, and the wit that filled a room comes back a step behind the rest of you.

choices.label: Pay the best physician in the city
choices.resultText: Barley water and Egyptian salves. You are yourself again by spring, nearly. The physician's bill is not nearly anything.

choices.label: Endure it and keep the salon open
choices.resultText: You host through the fever. Nobody notices the slowness but you, and you notice it every night.
